Let me analyze the teaching examples more carefully to identify the systematic errors and correction rules.

Looking at Example 1 (2025-03-06):
- History: Prices declining from ~83 down to ~68.5 over 18 days
- Model forecasts: Starting at 68.86 (I need to look at what the "Model Forecast (to be refined)" shows vs what was in the teaching examples)

From the teaching examples, the model forecasts were too high compared to true outcomes in Example 1:
- Model: [67.43, 68.75, 69.10, 68.47, 69.91, 71.11, 71.46, 70.68, 72.14, 74.63, 74.80, 73.77, 74.33, 73.70, 74.33, 72.21, 72.55, 72.02, 74.24, 73.24, 70.82, 68.49, 67.48, 66.77, 65.60, 66.80, 69.45, 70.84, 70.19, 70.59]
- True: [67.32, 68.63, 69.01, 68.24, 69.62, 70.60, 70.99, 70.11, 71.30, 73.44, 73.01, 71.45, 71.52, 70.46, 70.83, 68.54, 68.80, 67.98, 69.86, 68.55, 66.06, 63.82, 62.84, 62.06, 60.94, 62.12, 64.82, 66.51, 66.19, 66.97]

Looking at the divergence:
- Days 0-3: Model is about 0.1-0.3 too high


- Days 4-9: Model becomes significantly too high, ranging from 0.3 to 2.0 above true values
- Days 10-14: Discrepancy remains notable, with model values exceeding true outcomes by 0.2 to 1.2
- Days 15-18: Model forecasts start converging closer to true values,
